solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Successful president hard worker, Irish leader admitted

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so only the opening letter of Irish is wanted
something admitted is let inside, so this letter goes within the president's name

blocks.note: Donald Trump, US president
first letter of Irish
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
the worker ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: A successful president and a hard-working Irish leader are taken into the fold.
explanation.walkthrough: Hard is the pencil-grade abbreviation, and the ant is the crossword's usual worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Triumphant describes someone who has won or achieved a victory, which is being successful.

clue.text: The best place to go for a spin

indicators.note: spinning turns something round, so the word for place is read the other way

blocks.note: a spot is a place

explanation.surface: Someone recommends the finest spot for a drive in the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go for a spin' reads like a car outing; here it turns SPOT around.
explanation.definitionFit: Tops is informal for excellent or first-rate, as in 'that film is the tops'.

clue.text: I published one article for The National

definitions.note: a noun: a citizen of a country

blocks.note: taken as written
a paper ran a story when it published it
Roman numeral one
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A journalist boasts of placing a piece in The National, a Scottish newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The National looks like the newspaper's title, but the definition is just a national of one country.
explanation.definitionFit: An Iranian is a citizen of Iran, one example of a national of a particular country.

clue.text: Punchy types delighted with swim after training

indicators.note: training reshapes and rearranges, so the letters are put into new order

blocks.note: taken as written, part of the fodder
taken as written, the rest of the fodder

explanation.surface: Energetic people are thrilled to have a swim after their workout.
explanation.definitionFit: Middleweights are boxers in a mid-range weight class, and boxers throw punches for a living.

clue.text: Mostly dislike fights with dukes in Balmoral accommodation

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: to hate is to dislike strongly
dukes is old slang for fists, and someone who fights with fists boxes

explanation.surface: Someone dislikes the brawls involving aristocrats staying at the royal estate in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Balmoral suggests the royal castle, but a balmoral is also a Scottish brimless bonnet; dukes here are fists, not nobles.
explanation.definitionFit: A balmoral is a kind of cap, and hatboxes are the cases that store headwear.

clue.text: Big bangers northern music producer finally records

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word records

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for northern
a uke, or ukulele, is an instrument that produces music
last letter of records

explanation.surface: A northern record producer's last album was a smash hit.
explanation.walkthrough: Music producer suggests a person in a studio; it is an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuclear weapons produce the biggest explosions there are, so they are jokingly big bangers.

clue.text: Dull retrospective look at lyricist

indicators.note: a retrospective look goes backwards in time, so the word is read from its end

blocks.note: a bard is a poet or songwriter

explanation.surface: A critic finds a career retrospective of a songwriter boring.
explanation.definitionFit: Drab means dreary and colourless, the same as dull in the sense of lacking interest.

clue.text: Detachment of soldiers kept in the rear?

blocks.note: first meaning: emotional coolness or aloofness
second meaning: troops held back from the front line for later use

explanation.surface: A military unit is held back behind the lines.
explanation.walkthrough: Detachment reads as a military unit, joining the soldiers; it is really the personal quality of aloofness.
explanation.definitionFit: Reserve names both a cool, restrained manner and the part of an army withheld from action.

clue.text: A long nibble on Rod’s lolly

blocks.note: lolly and bread are both British slang for money
a rod is a stick

explanation.surface: Someone takes a long lick of Rod's ice lolly.
explanation.walkthrough: Lolly suggests a lollipop or ice lolly, but in British slang it means cash, as does bread; the possessive just orders the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A breadstick is a long, thin, crisp stick of baked dough eaten as a snack.

clue.text: Quiet boy clutching bit of itchy cloth

indicators.note: to clutch is to hold tight, so one word wraps round another
just a bit, meaning only the opening letter of itchy

blocks.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
a lad is a boy
first letter of itchy

explanation.surface: A shy boy holds on to a scratchy piece of fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: Quiet is the musical direction piano, written p.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaid is a woven tartan fabric, so it is a type of cloth.

clue.text: Disagree with kidnap?

definitions.note: read cryptically as two words: to take someone's child

blocks.note: first meaning: the idiom for objecting to a point
second meaning: issue means offspring, so taking issue is snatching a child

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second reading, where issue means children.
explanation.definitionFit: To take issue is an idiom for objecting; issue also means offspring, so literally taking them is abducting.

clue.text: Unspecified dinner and teatime must be sorted out

indicators.note: sorting out a mess puts things into a fresh order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, part of the fodder
taken as written, the rest of the fodder

explanation.surface: A household has yet to fix when the evening meal and tea will happen.
explanation.definitionFit: Indeterminate means not fixed or not stated exactly, which is what unspecified also conveys.

clue.text: Sick prisoner embarrassed about minor rash

blocks.note: ill means sick
a con is a convict
minor, as in a side issue or side road
red in the face from embarrassment

explanation.surface: An ill inmate is ashamed of a small skin complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: Rash looks like a skin condition but is the adjective meaning hasty; the embarrassment is about the minor thing, so it is placed after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-considered means done without proper thought, which is what a rash decision is.

clue.text: Needing to get fixed up, as in ripped jeans?

definitions.note: plural noun, a style of tight trousers

indicators.note: fixing something up means repairing and reworking it, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Torn denim is in need of mending.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface also evokes leaking pipes needing a plumber, apt for the answer's other sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Drainpipes are very narrow-legged trousers, often made as skinny jeans, named for their pipe-like shape.

clue.text: Famous soldiers had to keep close to Napoleon

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only the final letter of Napoleon counts
keeping something means holding it within, so one letter sits inside the others

blocks.note: RE, the Royal Engineers
had in the sense of possessed
final letter of Napoleon

explanation.surface: Celebrated troops held their position close to the French emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: Close to looks like nearness, but it means the end letter; the Royal Engineers are the soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Renowned means widely known and celebrated, a straightforward synonym for famous.

clue.text: A trial involving one leading tense witness

indicators.note: involving means taking something in, so one letter goes inside the trial word
the one in the lead is at the front, so just the first letter of tense

blocks.note: taken as written
a test is a trial
first letter of tense

explanation.surface: A nervous key witness takes the stand in a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: One leading tense means the first letter of tense, which goes just inside the trial word.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to bear witness or certify that something is true, so it is the verb witness.

clue.text: We’re against folk who assume work comes first!

indicators.note: comes first says which of the two pieces is placed ahead of the other

blocks.note: op, short for opus, a musical work
posers assume airs or attitudes

explanation.surface: Protesters declare their opposition to people who think their job matters most.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is spoken by the answer itself: those who say 'we're against' are opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposers are people who object or resist, the group who would declare themselves against something.

clue.text: Where you must write a woman’s name

blocks.note: first meaning, as two words: a solver writes answers inside the crossword lattice
second meaning: a Scandinavian girl's name, as in the actress Bergman

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a self-referential nod to the crossword itself: letters go in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Split in two it says where crossword letters belong; as one word it is a familiar female first name.

clue.text: Wild orgies ultimately attract complaints

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters run riot into a new order
ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter of attract

blocks.note: taken as written, the main fodder
last letter of attract

explanation.surface: Debauched parties eventually draw criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: Complaints suggests grumbles, but it is the medical sense: ailments.
explanation.definitionFit: A goitre is a swelling of the thyroid gland, and complaint is a standard word for a bodily ailment.

clue.text: Histrionic English singer captured in old snap

indicators.note: something captured in a picture sits inside it, so those letters go within the photo word

blocks.note: o is a standard abbreviation for old
a snap is a photo, or pic
standard abbreviation
an informer who sings to the police is a rat

explanation.surface: A dramatic English vocalist is caught in a vintage photo.
explanation.walkthrough: Singer suggests a vocalist, but in crime slang it is an informer who sings to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Operatic in the figurative sense means extravagantly dramatic, the same exaggerated quality histrionic describes.

clue.text: Case of the right drinking wine’s more yummy

indicators.note: a case is the outside shell, so only the outer letters of the word the
drinking takes something inside, so the wine goes within the other letters

blocks.note: outer letters of the
standard abbreviation for right
Asti is an Italian sparkling wine

explanation.surface: A wine glass of the correct sort makes a drink taste better.
explanation.walkthrough: Case of the means just the outer letters of the; the wine is the Italian sparkling one from Piedmont.
explanation.definitionFit: Tastier means having more flavour, the comparative of tasty, which matches more yummy.

clue.text: Musical groups performing in Polish march

indicators.note: performing puts things through their paces, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder, every letter used

explanation.surface: Orchestras are playing a march in Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: A philharmonic is a symphony orchestra, so several of them are large ensembles of musicians.

clue.text: Wine with port punch getting bishop out of it

indicators.note: removing the bishop from it means dropping that letter from the punch word

blocks.note: Rio de Janeiro, a major port
a jab is a quick punch
B, the chess notation for bishop, is removed

explanation.surface: A wine is served alongside port and a punch bowl that sent a churchman reeling.
explanation.walkthrough: Port and punch look like drinks beside the wine; they are a harbour city and a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red or white wine from the Rioja region of northern Spain.

clue.text: Now listen to sounds

indicators.note: sounds says the word is wanted by its pronunciation, not its spelling

blocks.note: to listen to is to hear

explanation.surface: An instruction to pay attention to the noises at this moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Here can mean at this point or at this moment, as in 'here we go', so it works for now.

clue.text: Recipe sop cooked up for looker in the Navy

indicators.note: cooking up mixes ingredients into something new, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder, every letter used

explanation.surface: A soggy dish is prepared for a good-looking sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: Looker suggests an attractive person; here it is a device that looks.
explanation.definitionFit: A submarine's periscope is the tube through which naval crews look above the surface.

clue.text: A team apart

blocks.note: taken as written
a side is a team

explanation.walkthrough: 'A team' reads as one phrase, the best squad, but splits into A plus a word for team.
explanation.definitionFit: Aside means to one side or apart, as in setting something aside or joking aside.

clue.text: Sauce with special forces people to have drop of Spa

indicators.note: a drop is a tiny amount, so only the first letter of Spa

blocks.note: the SAS, Britain's Special Air Service
first letter of Spa

explanation.surface: Elite soldiers take a sip of mineral water with their condiment.
explanation.walkthrough: Sauce looks like a condiment, but it means cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauce is informal for impudence or cheek, and sass is the American slang for the same backchat.

clue.text: Feel shares must go up without any problem

indicators.note: going up in smoke or being blown up scatters things, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder, every letter used

explanation.surface: An investor senses stock prices will rise without trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Go up sounds like a share price rising; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Hassle-free means free of bother or difficulty, which is doing something without trouble.
